segments.title: Chương 150
segments.content:
Chapter 153: Happy Farm Goes Live: Can't Stop Thinking About Harvesting Crops

Another day, Lin Dongliang and Chen Guiliang signed a non-disclosure agreement, and ByteDance submitted its core company data to IDG.

Lin Dongliang said in a joking tone, "How about we sign Game Science as well?"

Chen Guiliang politely declined, "Let's talk about it next time we're short on money."

Lin Dongliang said, "In three days, IDG will send someone over to verify the data you've provided. I have some business in Hong Kong, so I'll be leaving Xiao He in charge here for now."

"We'll be troubling Ms. He, then," said Chen Guiliang.

He Fang smiled slightly. "I hope we have a pleasant collaboration."

Just then, Ao Yanchen knocked on the conference room door. "CEO Chen, Mr. Fu Jixun from DJ is here."

He Fang frowned upon hearing this.

Lin Dongliang, however, broke into a smile, though it was a little unnatural.

Fu Jixun's claim to fame was leading the investment in KongZhong.

Younger people might not know KongZhong, but it was once the most profitable internet company in China. Two years ago, its MMS and WAP revenues were both number one in the country, and at the time, it had surpassed QQ to become Monternet's largest client.

The NDA was already signed. Chen Guiliang excused himself and went out to meet Fu Jixun from DJ.

Lin Dongliang quickly followed.

Wang Kai was in another reception room, chatting very enthusiastically with Fu Jixun.

"Mr. Fu, CEO Chen is here," Ao Yanchen said.

Fu Jixun was about to stand up for a handshake when he saw Lin Dongliang behind Chen Guiliang.

Lin Dongliang shot Fu Jixun a look, and Fu Jixun nodded in understanding.

When two venture capital firms ran into each other, they would rarely compete; instead, they would usually invest jointly.

Of course, if a project was particularly promising, they would privately fight for the dominant position to decide who would lead the investment and who would follow.

For incredibly popular projects or those with huge funding amounts, it was even possible to have two lead investors and a whole group of follow-on investors.

As if just going through the motions, Fu Jixun had a preliminary meeting with Chen Guiliang and Guo Feng, then took his leave in less than an hour.

Wang Kai was already overjoyed, saying to Chen Guiliang, "Two VCs coming at the same time, Xiaonei is a hot ticket for capital!"

"It's all thanks to the support of Professor Wang and the Peking University Science Park," Chen Guiliang said, offering a casual compliment.

Wang Kai was quite pleased. "I'm just doing my job, serving the entrepreneurial teachers and students. It's because you've done such a good job with the project that you've attracted so many VCs."

Chen Guiliang painted a rosy picture, "When we go public, we will definitely show our immense gratitude."

"Just treating me to a barbecue outside the south gate of Peking University will be enough. Don't take the opportunity to corrupt me," Wang Kai said with a righteous expression, but his eyes were full of anticipation.

Chen Guiliang quickly said, "How could that be called corruption? It will certainly be legal and compliant."

Wang Kai became even more enthusiastic. "After you get the venture capital, submit a document to me. I'll help you apply for the 'three years tax-free, two years half-tax' incentive!"

"Professor Wang is truly a great mentor and friend to us student entrepreneurs!" Chen Guiliang exclaimed with sincere gratitude.

Lin Dongliang and Fu Jixun chose a coffee shop.

"Why are you here too?" Lin Dongliang asked.

Fu Jixun smiled. "If you can come, why can't I?"

Lin Dongliang said, "There's a first-come, first-served principle to everything. I must be the lead investor on this project."

"You're that optimistic about it?" Fu Jixun asked.

Lin Dongliang said, "I'm optimistic about the founder."

"I'm optimistic about Xiaonei's 800,000 student users," Fu Jixun said. "Twelve days ago, they announced they'd broken 700,000 registered users, and four days ago, they announced they'd broken 800,000. That's a 100,000 user increase in just eight days."

Following the story chain, three-line poems, and the "The Wind Rises" combo, Xiaonei continued to ferment across major universities.

Using Xiaonei had now become a trend among university students.

It was undergoing rapid fission!

To be on the safe side, Guo Feng had just recently upgraded the servers to the one-million-user level.

It probably wouldn't be long before they'd need to upgrade the servers and bandwidth again.

The website's operating costs were increasing significantly.

"How much equity do you want?" Lin Dongliang asked.

Fu Jixun said, "At least 15%."

"Impossible. If you take 15% and I take 20%, that's 35% in total," Lin Dongliang said. "Chen Guiliang won't agree. And even if he did, I wouldn't. It would affect the Series B round!"

A Series A funding round below 15% not only solidified the founder's control but also made it more attractive for Series B investors to come on board.

A Series A between 15% and 25% was standard procedure and was the case most of the time.

A Series A between 25% and 35% meant the founder would have to implement a dual-class stock structure, and it would make things very difficult for Series B investors.

If Series A exceeded 35%, it would inevitably raise the difficulty of the Series B round to hell-level, and subsequent investors might even demand the founder buy back the Series A shares.

Fu Jixun asked, "IDG China has been throwing money around everywhere these past two years. How much capital do you guys have left?"

"Our funds are very ample," Lin Dongliang said.

These two were fighting for the lead position. The one forced to compromise would definitely have their Series A stake be less than 8%.

Chen Guiliang couldn't be bothered with how they negotiated. He didn't even participate in IDG's initial due diligence, merely sending Senior Ao to liaise with He Fang.

Kings deal with kings, generals with generals.

Only when Lin Dongliang appeared would Chen Guiliang appear; letting Senior Ao handle He Fang was more than enough.

Chen Guiliang had started to develop a love for learning. He attended classes diligently every day, and whenever he had time, he wrote the follow-up content for *Those Things in the Ming Dynasty*.

He even made plans with Bian Guanyue to visit Zhongshan Park together over the weekend.

"Did you become a school celebrity after 'The Wind Rises' was uploaded?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"Sigh!"

Bian Guanyue let out a sigh. "I was already a school celebrity last year when I was voted campus belle. My English teacher is a文艺女青年, and she even asked me a few days ago if I was the one who sang 'The Wind Rises'."

"Not bad, your teacher is a fan," Chen Guiliang laughed.

"I told you I should've used a stage name," Bian Guanyue said. "Li Jing is such a great name. I guarantee no one would have recognized me."

Chen Guiliang asked curiously, "Why did you have to use Li Jing, and not Zhang Jing or Wang Jing?"

Bian Guanyue said, "When I was studying in Rongcheng, I had a good friend named Li Jing."

The two of them arrived in front of the bronze statue of Sun Yat-sen and took a picture for each other.

"Excuse me, sir, could you help take a picture for us?" Chen Guiliang called out to a tourist.

The tourist was traveling with his whole family. He picked up the digital camera and studied it. "Is this the shutter?"

Chen Guiliang said, "That's right, just press it. It's even simpler than a film camera. Just press away, it doesn't use up any film."

The man took several shots and reviewed the photos with his wife.

His wife said, "This is really convenient. Maybe we should buy one too?"

The man asked, "Young man, how much did this camera of yours cost?"

"Over 3,000 yuan. I bought it last year, so it should be cheaper this year," Chen Guiliang said as he took the camera back. "Thanks."

"You're welcome."

The two continued to stroll inside, taking pictures whenever they came across a scenic spot.

Bian Guanyue was having a wonderful time. "I want to get these photos developed, along with the ones from last year's National Day, and mail them to my grandparents. They'll definitely be very happy!"

"Sure, I'll mail a few home too," Chen Guiliang said.

His parents didn't have cell phones, and there wasn't even a landline in the entire village.

There was a teahouse next to the village committee office where you could pay to use the owner's cell phone.

In all his time at university, Chen Guiliang had only spoken to his parents on the phone four times. It was mainly because his parents worried about the cost, thinking long-distance calls were too expensive.

As they rested on a bench near the Altar of Land and Grain, Bian Guanyue said, "Are there any amusement parks in Beijing?"

"I'll ask around when I get back," Chen Guiliang teased. "You're still playing at amusement parks at your age? Want to ride the carousel together?"

"Okay," Bian Guanyue said with considerable anticipation.

While the two of them were enjoying themselves, He Fang was getting a little anxious.

ByteDance was just a small startup; the preliminary due diligence was completed in a single day. He Fang wanted to arrange for formal negotiations, but Chen Guiliang was playing hard to get, only having Ao Yanchen stall her.

"When exactly is your CEO Chen free?" He Fang was almost out of patience.

Ao Yanchen smiled. "Ms. He, why don't you wait and see what happens tonight?"

"Are you guys launching another event?" He Fang asked.

Ao Yanchen said, "Game Science made a mini-game and has authorized ByteDance to operate it on their behalf."

He Fang thought to herself: Playing this left-hand-to-right-hand trick again. I must add a restrictive clause when we sign the agreement!

In the evening, Ao Yanchen invited He Fang to have a work meal at the cafeteria.

They returned to the company and waited until eight o'clock at night. Ao Yanchen said, "We've upgraded our servers and bandwidth again for this game."

"Are you that certain so many people will play it?" He Fang felt that the people at this company were all very confident.

So confident it bordered on conceited.

Ao Yanchen logged into her own Xiaonei account. "Ms. He, would you like to give it a try?"

"Happy Farm?" He Fang curiously checked the gameplay instructions, then began to till the soil and plant vegetables.

Ao Yanchen directed from the side, "Xiaonei has already launched a top-up system. Besides buying things like letter paper, Xiaonei Coins can also be used to buy items in Happy Farm. I have money in my Xiaonei account, you can check the in-game store yourself."

He Fang clicked into the store and saw all sorts of seeds, as well as items like fertilizer. She could also directly click on unlocked plots to buy land and expand her farm.

She tried out all kinds of items and was soon immersed in the world of a farm owner.

A while later, Ao Yanchen reminded her, "You can go to your friends' farms to steal their crops."

He Fang quickly clicked on Ao Yanchen's Xiaonei friends, visiting more than ten farms in a row, until she finally found a patch of crops that was ripe but hadn't been harvested yet.

She quickly stole it.

He Fang felt a great sense of accomplishment, and it was especially thrilling.

Just then, a message came from the friend whose crops she had stolen: "Ao Yanchen, you thief, give me back my bok choy!"

"Haha..."

He Fang burst out laughing, then felt it was a bit unladylike and quickly composed herself before continuing her search for crops to steal.

That night, countless students couldn't sleep soundly.

Some even set alarms to wake up in the middle of the night to steal crops.

When He Fang returned to her hotel, she called Lin Dongliang. "Game Science made a mini-game and let Xiaonei operate it."

"Does it have market potential?" Lin Dongliang asked.

He Fang said, "I think I'm addicted. All I can think about right now is harvesting crops."

Lin Dongliang: "..."

(End of Chapter)
